title: Shanghai: One River Splits 1920s Europe From the Future | China Travel Expert
description:
One river in Shanghai separates two centuries. Which bank would you walk first?

On the west bank stands the Bund — a row of 1920s banks and trading houses in Gothic, Neoclassical and Art Deco stone, nicknamed "the museum of buildings" when it was the financial heart of Asia. Straight across the Huangpu, Lujiazui was still farmland, warehouses and low houses in 1990. After it became a special zone in 1992, the Oriental Pearl went up in 1994 — and today the skyline stacks the world's first trio of adjacent supertall towers, topped by the 632-metre Shanghai Tower. A whole future built in about thirty years, facing a century-old one across the water.

🧭 Expert Tip: Skip the pricey river cruise — the local Huangpu public ferry crosses for pocket change with the same skyline. Come at blue hour for both banks lit at once.

一条黄浦江，一岸1920年代的万国建筑，一岸三十年长出的天际线。
